steps.text: A similar question. Which of these terms is not a number system?
Ask the same question of every term: what is it?
steps.visual:
binary: base 2
denary: base 10    hexadecimal: base 16
pixel: ?

steps.text: A pixel is one dot of an image. It is not a way of writing numbers, so it is the odd one out.
steps.visual: pixel: a dot of an image

steps.text: Your part (a): ask of each term: does it say how the bits travel (how many wires, which direction)? Or does it do a different job?
steps.visual: how the bits travel, or another job?

steps.text: A similar question. State one drawback of using parallel rather than serial data transmission.
A drawback of one method is something the other method does better. Serial sends one bit at a time, so the bits stay in order over a long distance.
steps.visual: serial does better: bits stay in order over a long way

steps.text: So a drawback of parallel: over a long distance, its bits can arrive at different times (skew).
steps.visual: Drawback of parallel: the bits can skew

steps.text: Your part (b): what does parallel do better than serial? The drawback of serial is the other side of that.
steps.visual: what parallel does better → what serial gives up

steps.label: Command Words: What the Question Wants
steps.content:
Command Words: What the Question Wants

Think → Pair → SharePredict: two students answer "Explain why a file is sent as packets. [2]". One writes one fact. The other writes a fact, then "so ..." and a second fact. Which gets 2 marks? Why?Show the worked answer

The second. Explain wants a point and the reason or result that follows from it.

"So" or "because" joins the two marks together.

  • Identify, State, Give: a short answer. One point for each mark.
  • Describe: say what happens, step by step.
  • Explain: say what happens and why. Use "so" or "because".
  • Justify: choose, then give reasons that fit this scenario.
  • Count the marks: [3] means three different points.
Explain why a file is sent as packets. [2]
If one packet is lost, only that packet is sent again. 1 mark
... so the whole file does not need to be sent again. 1 mark

steps.label: Choosing a Method: Three Questions
steps.content:
Choosing a Method: Three Questions

Think → Pair → SharePredict: a rain sensor sends readings to a computer in another building. The computer never sends anything back. Which method fits? Why?Show the worked answer

Serial simplex. Another building is far away, so serial: the bits arrive in order.

Data only goes one way, so simplex.

  • 1. How far? Far (another room or building, more than about 5 m): serial. The bits arrive in order, with less interference.
  • Very short, and speed matters: parallel. It is faster.
  • 2. Which way? One way only: simplex. Both ways, one at a time: half-duplex. Both ways at the same time: full-duplex.
  • 3. Justify: link every choice to words in the scenario, such as "another room" or "sends back".
Far away? → serial
Very short and fast? → parallel
One way only? → simplex
Both ways, taking turns? → half-duplex
Both ways at once? → full-duplex

steps.label: Compare: One Way or Both Ways?
steps.content:
Compare: One Way or Both Ways?

Think → Pair → ShareBoth links are long distance, so both use serial. Predict the direction for each one. Which words in the scenario decide it?Show the answer

Left: "never sends anything back", so simplex.

Right: "both talk ... at the same time", so full-duplex.

A rain sensor on a roof

Sends readings to a computer in another building.
The computer never sends anything back.

serial simplex

A video call

The two computers are in different cities.
Both people talk at the same time.

serial full-duplex

  • The same distance gives the same first word: serial.
  • Who sends, and when, gives the second word. Quote those words in your reasons.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2023, Question 5(b)(i). A website allows users to purchase items. Computer A sends a request for the homepage to the website's server. Computer A needs to be directly connected to a router that is located in a different room.

items.prompt: Choose serial data transmission or parallel data transmission for this connection. Explain the reasons for your choice.
items.modelAnswer: Serial. The router is in another room, so the data travels a longer distance. The data arrives in the order it was sent, and is less likely to have interference.
scheme: serial: data arrives in the order sent // does not need reordering
serial: less likely to experience interference
serial: ... less likely to have errors
serial: can transmit over a longer distance (another room)
serial: still fast transmission ...
serial: ... sufficient for this purpose
parallel: faster transmission speed than serial
parallel: ... faster response to requests
parallel: very long connection not needed
parallel: ... the next room is (likely) within distance for parallel
parallel: ... unlikely to error / arrive out of sequence / skew
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2023, Question 5(b)(i). A website allows users to purchase items. Computer A sends a request for the homepage to the website's server. Computer A needs to be directly connected to a router that is located in a different room. Marking rule: No mark for the choice. Three from, for reasons that match the choice, one mark for each point met, up to 3.

steps.label: Choosing: Why Serial Simplex?
steps.content:
Choosing: Why Serial Simplex?

Each word is a separate choice. Reasons for only one of them can leave marks behind.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2024, Question 5(b)(ii). A barcode scanning system uses a check digit to check for errors in data on input. After a barcode is scanned, data is sent to a stock control system to update the stock value stored for that product. The data is sent to the stock control system using serial simplex data transmission.

items.prompt: Explain why serial simplex is the most appropriate method of data transmission for this purpose.
items.modelAnswer: The stock control system may be a long distance away, and serial is more reliable over a long distance. No reply is needed from the stock control system.
scheme: the stock control system may be a long distance away
... parallel should not be used in long distance transmission // serial is more reliable for long distance transmission
the data does not need to be sent quickly
... the increased speed of parallel is not needed
... as only small amounts of data need to be sent
the bits are sent / arrive in order
... the data will not be skewed // the data could be skewed if parallel was used
... there will be no data collisions
there will be less interference / crosstalk (due to single wire)
... there will be fewer errors in the data
no need for a reply / response from the stock control system
... half-duplex / full-duplex is not necessary as only one way transmission is needed
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2024, Question 5(b)(ii). A barcode scanning system uses a check digit to check for errors in data on input. After a barcode is scanned, data is sent to a stock control system to update the stock value stored for that product. The data is sent to the stock control system using serial simplex data transmission. Marking rule: Any three from, one mark for each point met, up to 3.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2024, Question 4(c). Data packets are transmitted across a network. Explain why serial data transmission is used to transmit the data packets.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: “Serial is faster than parallel, and it is cheaper because it uses one wire.”
This answer gets 0 marks. Write a better answer that gets 3 marks.
items.modelAnswer: The network may be spread over a long distance. The bits arrive in sequence, so they are less likely to be skewed.
scheme: the network may be spread over a long distance ...
... so it is more reliable
bits will be sent / arrive in sequence
... so bits are less likely to be skewed
less crosstalk / interference
... so less likely to have errors
the data may not need to be transmitted at a fast speed // the data transmission speed of serial is adequate
the cables in the network only use serial transmission
items.ariaLabel: Explain why serial data transmission is used to transmit the data packets. (better answer)
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2024, Question 4(c). Data packets are transmitted across a network. Explain why serial data transmission is used to transmit the data packets. A student wrote: "Serial is faster than parallel, and it is cheaper because it uses one wire." This got 0 of 3 marks: serial is slower than parallel, and "cheaper" is not in the mark scheme. The student now writes a better answer. Marking rule: Any three from, one mark for each point met, up to 3.
